paper_metadata.title: Risk factors for seizure recurrence in children after first unprovoked seizure

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study provides clear inclusion/exclusion criteria and describes the recruitment setting and period. However, it is a single-center study with a relatively small sample size (n=73), and there is no information regarding the total number of eligible patients versus those who actually participated, making it difficult to rule out selection bias.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Eligible candidates were children between 1 month and 15 years old who presented with their first unprovoked afebrile seizure.
items.reasoning: The target population is clearly defined by age and clinical presentation.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Participants were recruited from University of Yamanashi Hospital between 1 July 1997, and 30 June 2009.
items.reasoning: The recruitment site and dates are clear, but the specific method of identification (e.g., consecutive vs. convenience) is not explicitly stated.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: between 1 July 1997, and 30 June 2009.
items.reasoning: The dates are precisely provided.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: University of Yamanashi Hospital
items.reasoning: The specific hospital is named.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Exclusion criteria were ambiguous episodes, seizures occurring with acute encephalopathy... or presence of organic brain lesions on MRI... children with status epilepticus (defined as a seizure lasting >30 min... ) were also excluded.
items.reasoning: Detailed inclusion and exclusion criteria are provided, including specific definitions for 'unprovoked' and 'status epilepticus'.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 81 children met all entry criteria and underwent EEG. Eight were excluded because no follow up was obtained after first unprovoked seizure. Thus data were analyzed for 73 children.
items.reasoning: While the flow of the 81 identified children is clear, the paper does not state how many children presented to the hospital with a first seizure but were not recruited, making the participation rate of the total eligible population unknown.

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: Candidates were children between 3 months and 13 years old (mean age, 4.3 years; infants, n = 12; toddlers, n = 47; school children, n = 14).
items.reasoning: Age, sex, neurodevelopmental status, and family history are described in the results and Table 1.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The attrition rate was approximately 10% (8/81), which is acceptable. The study ensured a minimum 2-year follow-up for all analyzed participants, and the reasons for exclusion (lack of follow-up) were stated.

items.reasoning: 90% of the eligible sample was analyzed, which is a high completion rate.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (seizure type and EEG) were defined using international standards (ILAE) and measured using objective methods (EEG) with a clear protocol for interpretation.

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: Seizures were classified as generalized tonic or tonic–clonic, atonic, simple partial, complex partial, or partial secondarily generalized in accordance with International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) criteria.
items.reasoning: Standardized ILAE criteria were used for seizure classification.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF
items.prompt: Method of PF measurement is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: EEG reports were reviewed by one of three authors... all difficult or borderline EEG were reviewed by at least two interpreters.
items.reasoning: The use of multiple reviewers for difficult cases increases the reliability of the EEG interpretation.

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: Candidates were children between 1 month and 15 years old
items.reasoning: Age was treated as a categorical variable in some descriptions but the primary PFs (EEG/Seizure type) are naturally categorical.

items.label: Method and Setting of PF Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of measurement of PF is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: EEG was performed for all subjects using a 10- or 20-channel machine with the 10–20 electrode system.
items.reasoning: A standardized protocol was applied to all participants.

items.label: Proportion of data on PF available for analysis
items.prompt: Adequate proportion of the study sample has complete data for PF variable.
items.evidence_snippet: A total of 81 children met all entry criteria and underwent EEG.
items.reasoning: All participants included in the analysis had the prognostic factor (EEG) measured.

items.label: Method used for missing data
items.prompt: Appropriate methods of imputation are used for missing 'PF' data.
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text
items.reasoning: There was no missing PF data for the analyzed cohort, so imputation was not required.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The outcome (seizure recurrence) is clearly defined and was monitored through regular clinical follow-up and interviews, which is standard for this type of study.

items.label: Definition of the Outcome
items.prompt: A clear definition of outcome is provided, including duration of follow-up and level and extent of the outcome construct.
items.evidence_snippet: Recurrence was defined as any unprovoked seizure occurring >24 h after the first seizure.
items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined with a temporal threshold.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome
items.prompt: The method of outcome measurement used is adequately valid and reliable to limit misclassification bias (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and confirmation of outcome with valid and reliable test).
items.evidence_snippet: patients were monitored by means of regular visits or telephone interviews at least every 3 months
items.reasoning: Frequent monitoring (every 3 months) reduces recall bias for the occurrence of a second seizure.

items.label: Method and Setting of Outcome Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of outcome measurement is the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: After enrollment, patients were monitored by means of regular visits or telephone interviews at least every 3 months
items.reasoning: The follow-up protocol was standardized for the cohort.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: While the study mentions multivariate analysis in the discussion, the results section primarily reports univariate (log-rank) results. The small sample size limits the ability to adjust for multiple confounders simultaneously.
